stem:
A $0.50\text{ g}$ sample of a Group 2 metal, $\mathbf{M}$, was added to $40.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $1.00\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid (an excess).

equation 1 $$\mathbf{M}(\text{s}) + 2\text{HCl}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \mathbf{M}\text{Cl}_2(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_2(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of hydrochloric acid present in $40.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $1.00\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
When the reaction had finished, the resulting solution was made up to $100\text{ cm}^3$ in a volumetric flask.

A $10.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample of the solution from the volumetric flask required $15.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.050\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sodium carbonate solution, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, for complete neutralisation of the remaining hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write the equation for the complete reaction of sodium carbonate with hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of sodium carbonate needed to react with the hydrochloric acid in the $10.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample from the volumetric flask.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of hydrochloric acid in the $10.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Calculate the total amount, in moles, of hydrochloric acid remaining after the reaction shown in equation 1.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Use your answers to (a) and (b)(iv) to calculate the amount, in moles, of hydrochloric acid that reacted with the $0.50\text{ g}$ sample of $\mathbf{M}$.

parts.label: (b)(vi)
parts.text: Use your answer to (v) and equation 1 to calculate the amount, in moles, of $\mathbf{M}$ in the $0.50\text{ g}$ sample.

parts.label: (b)(vii)
parts.text: Calculate the relative atomic mass, $A_{\text{r}}$, of $\mathbf{M}$ and identify $\mathbf{M}$.
